title: EXP-017 — Visible FormSync View Output Semantics
objective: Using the existing factory-owned User-scoped FX_FormVariableLab05 only as a read-only target, open Runtime FormSync through the supported UI, select the intended Source configuration, isolate exactly the target Form and scope, then use only visibly rendered Script-tab controls to select View and record the visible state of Script form license before generating once. Prove whether Generate visibly opens the documented temporary View representation. If the required View control cannot be visibly selected, or Generate instead produces only file/download behavior without a visible temporary representation, record that exact result and stop; do not manipulate hidden controls, switch to Save, retry through alternate mechanisms, or investigate variable serialization.

in_scope: Read-only inspection of the existing FX_FormVariableLab05 User-scoped Form identity
Runtime FormSync using the already observed Source configuration and Filter Configuration=Source route
Filtering and including exactly one FX_FormVariableLab05 row after visibly verifying Name, Scope Type, and User/Group Name
Visible Script-tab inspection of Output=View, Output=Save, Generate, and Script form license state
One Generate action only after View is visibly selected through supported rendered UI
Capturing the actual visible post-Generate result, including a temporary View page if one appears
Closing the generated/output surface and rechecking the target Form identity read-only to confirm no Mongoose artifact was changed
out_of_scope: Form-variable creation, editing, saving, persistence, serialization, or runtime-value testing
Interpreting generic Variables/FormID SQL as evidence for any specific variable
Creating, editing, deleting, renaming, Saving, or Regenerating any Mongoose Form or component
Global-object unload, IDO-metadata unload, cache experiments, or User Preference changes
Direct database access, undocumented APIs, reverse-engineered payloads, internal Ext stores, or hidden-control manipulation

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Do not create, edit, delete, rename, Save, Regenerate, or execute any Mongoose artifact.
Do not create, edit, delete, or inspect the lifecycle of any Form variable.
Do not select Output=Save or intentionally cause file-output behavior.
Do not programmatically set, click, dispatch events to, or otherwise manipulate hidden/off-screen View, Save, Script form license, or Generate controls.
Do not use JavaScript, Ext internals, DOM property mutation, synthetic event dispatch, or internal stores to force Script-tab state.
Do not perform more than one Generate action.
Do not execute or apply generated SQL.
Do not invoke Unload All Global Form Objects, Regenerate Form, or change User Preferences.

Do not log in, Sign In/OK, deliberately reauthenticate, restart the browser, or replace the session after the experiment starts; after one fresh snapshot and one corrected inspection, treat an unusable session or UI as a blocker.

If View cannot be visibly selected through supported rendered UI, or the post-Generate result is not visibly the documented temporary View representation, stop and record the observed negative result without widening scope.

acceptance_checks.description: Before FormSync generation, evidence visibly proves a live session, the intended configuration context, and exactly the existing target Form identity FX_FormVariableLab05 at User scope; no session-establishment action occurs after experiment start.

FormSync Filter evidence visibly shows Filter Configuration=Source, Scope Type=User, the exact User/Group Name for the target row, and after Deselect All exactly one included row: FX_FormVariableLab05. The capture must show the decisive rendered grid state, not rely on hidden store data alone.

Before Generate, a screenshot visibly shows the rendered Script-tab Output state with View selected and Save not selected, and also visibly records the Script form license checkbox state. No hidden/off-screen/programmatic control mutation is used. If these states cannot be visibly established, the experiment is blocked before Generate.

Exactly one Generate action is performed through the visible supported control, and the immediate post-Generate evidence visibly shows the actual resulting UI. PASS requires a visible temporary FormSync View representation; a ZIP/download without such visible representation is recorded as an observed negative and does not satisfy this check.

If a visible temporary representation appears, evidence from that rendered representation visibly identifies FX_FormVariableLab05 or otherwise links the displayed output unambiguously to the single included scoped Form. No claim about any specific Form variable is permitted.

After closing the output/FormSync surface, read-only evidence rechecks FX_FormVariableLab05 as the same User-scoped target and records that no Form, variable, component, preference, or other Mongoose artifact was created, modified, Saved, Regenerated, deleted, executed, or applied during the experiment.
Final repository audit shows experiment changes confined to the EXP-017 record and evidence/EXP-017/; no recipe, environment file, AGENTS.md, unrelated experiment record, or factory code is modified.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261005-181911-K73K. Rationale: EXP-016 and EXP-016-R2 established a reproducible supported FormSync Script-generation route for an exact User-scoped Form, but EXP-016-R2 did not prove the documented Output=View semantic path: the View input was off-screen and changed programmatically, while Generate produced a ZIP. Before using FormSync output as a stronger serialization instrument, the smallest next step is a new read-only experiment using only visibly rendered supported FormSync controls to establish what Output=View actually does in this 2026.09.08 environment. This is a different documented approach, not a workaround for the blocked Form-variable lifecycle experiments.
